facts.statement: Albertaceratops is a centrosaurine horned dinosaur from the Upper Cretaceous of Alberta, Canada.
facts.quote: Albertaceratops (meaning "Alberta horned face") is a genus of centrosaurine horned dinosaur from the middle Campanian-age Upper Cretaceous Oldman Formation of Alberta, Canada.

facts.statement: Albertaceratops is distinguished by long, robust brow horns, a feature generally short in other centrosaurines.
facts.quote: Its most distinctive feature is the presence of long, robust brow horns, which are generally short in other centrosaurine dinosaurs.

facts.statement: Albertaceratops is unusual for combining long brow horns with the typical centrosaurine skull structure.
facts.quote: Albertaceratops is unusual in combining long brow horns with an otherwise centrosaurine skull, as centrosaurines normally possess short brow horns.

facts.statement: Albertaceratops is estimated to have reached a length of 5.8 meters and a mass of 3500 kilograms.
facts.quote: Its size has been estimated at 5.8 m and 3500 kg.

facts.statement: Albertaceratops possessed a bony ridge over its nose and two large, outwardly projecting hooks on its frill.
facts.quote: Over its nose was a bony ridge, and on its frill were two large outwardly-projecting hooks.

facts.statement: Albertaceratops is known primarily from a nearly complete skull, with limited information regarding the rest of its skeleton.
facts.quote: Albertaceratops was described on the basis of a nearly complete skull, while information about the rest of its skeleton, including its torso, remains limited.

facts.statement: The type specimen of Albertaceratops is a single complete skull found in August 2001, accompanied by skull and postcranial fragments.
facts.quote: Albertaceratops is known from a single complete skull (TMP.2001.26.1) found in August 2001 and skull and postcranial fragments.

facts.statement: The species name A. nesmoi honors Cecil Nesmo, a rancher from Manyberries, Alberta, who aided fossil hunters.
facts.quote: The specific name, A. nesmoi, is derived from the name of Cecil Nesmo, a rancher living in Manyberries, Alberta, a town of less than 100 people located 71 km south of Medicine Hat.

facts.statement: Phylogenetic analysis by Michael J. Ryan classifies Albertaceratops as the most basal member of the subfamily Centrosaurinae.
facts.quote: In a phylogenetic analysis by Michael J. Ryan, Albertaceratops was classified as the most basal member of Centrosaurinae.

facts.statement: Albertaceratops lived approximately 77.5 million years ago.
facts.quote: Both ceratopsids lived during the same time period, about 77.5 million years ago.

facts.statement: Albertaceratops lived during the Campanian stage of the Late Cretaceous, approximately between 84 and 71 million years ago.
facts.quote: que vivió a finales del Cretácico, hace aproximadamente entre 84 y 71 millones de años, el Campaniense, en lo que hoy es Norteamérica.

facts.statement: Michael J. Ryan's initial phylogenetic analysis identified Albertaceratops as a basal member of Centrosaurinae.
facts.quote: En el análisis filogenético inicial propuesto por su descriptor, Michael J. Ryan, lo encontró como un miembro basal de Centrosaurinae.

facts.statement: It is debated whether specimens from the Judith River Formation in Montana belong to Albertaceratops, as further study attributed them to the different centrosaurine Medusaceratops.
facts.quote: Additional specimens were reported from a bonebed in the Judith River Formation of Montana, which is equivalent to the Oldman Formation and differentiated only by the Canada–US border. However, further study showed these remains to come from a different centrosaurine, Medusaceratops.

rejected.statement: Instead of a prominent nasal horn, Albertaceratops had an elongated bony ridge on its snout and large outward projections on its neck frill.
rejected.quote: It also had an elongated bony ridge on its snout instead of a prominent nasal horn, as well as large projections extending outward from its neck frill.
